name: Kambera
catalog_quote: Main stress is always on the root-initial syllable (see below). [...] Full reduplication is the reduplication of the prosodic word i.e. a root plus possible affixes [...] [clitics] cannot be stressed i.e. they need a phonological host and do not form independent prosodic words.

audit.reasoning: Quote check: every load-bearing quotation in the record (Klamer 2005:710 twice, :712, :713, :731-2; van der Hulst & Klamer 1997:109) is present verbatim in the held PDFs at the stated pages (710 verified on PDF p.3 with printed header; the 1997 quote is p.109, as the owner review already corrected). Wielenga 1910:11 was re-checked against the archive.org scanned fetched sources now and matches, with one omitted clause (Wielenga flags marked exceptions with ^). Deciding source is a 2005 grammar sketch, but by the language's grammarian, post-dating her full grammar, and corroborated by two phonology papers we hold (1997, and 1996 now filed) that print stress marks on prefixed words (ka-'nga:u, ma-'la:, pa-'ndoi). Three independent statements by the describer agree: main stress exceptionless on the root-initial syllable, prefixes/proclitics unstressed inside the prosodic word, suffixes/paragogic -u str

sources.quote: Klamer 2005:710 (verified on page image): "Main stress is always on the root-initial syllable (see below)." and, same page: "Roots are disyllabic and main stress is without exception on the root-initial syllable. Only CVV and CV syllables can bear stress, CVC syllables are never stressed. Prefixes, suffixes and almost all clitics are unstressed." Supporting: van der Hulst & Klamer 1997:108: "(C)VV syllables can only occur under main stress - which is always on the first syllable of the root"; 19

sources.quote: Wielenga 1909:11 (Dutch): 'Stress: as a rule the stress falls on the penultimate syllable. Prefixes and suffixes exert no influence on this. The facultative closing oe [the paragogic /u/] does not count as a syllable — (wátar or wátaroe).' [For the exclusively disyllabic Kambera roots, penult-of-stem = initial-of-root, so Wielenga and Klamer state the same fact.]

sources.quote: '(2) a. pre-stress: /a/ (prefixes); b. primary stress: all vowels (first syllable of the root); c. post-stress: /i/, /a/, /u/ (second syllable of the root) ... Primary stress is on the first syllable of the root. Thus, (2a) implies that prefixes can only have the vowel /a/.' and '(C)VV syllables can only occur under main stress, i.e. as the first syllable of the root'.
